Distribution-network planning under load and outage uncertainty requires portfolios that remain useful as binding stresses change. SHIELD-MOEA combines non-dominated sorting, feasibility repair, selective worst-scenario screening, and disjoint scenario draws for search and evaluation. On a SimBench-derived benchmark with 72 candidate actions and five proxy objectives, its pooled mean hypervolume is 0.2740 over 30 seeds per stochastic method: 5.09% above NSGA-II with post-hoc repair and 5.56% above plain NSGA-II. Eight archived labels correspond to five active proxy configurations; four labels are independent seed blocks under identical ranges, and the configured DER multiplier is inactive in the implemented objectives. Across 1050 additional boundary runs, SHIELD-MOEA remains 3.46--7.20% above NSGA-II with repair within each tested budget, scenario-count, and survivability-coefficient setting. However, 441 fronts require low-side clipping, and clipping changes gap magnitude. Feasibility repair is the resolved performance mechanism; hybrid variation and periodic re-screening remain unresolved. Static code-path accounting attributes 65% fewer optimization-loop plan--scenario objective rows to screening, excluding reference-bound construction and held-out evaluation, but neither front quality nor archived wall-clock time improves against no screening. An illustrative 1296-case fixed-mapping AC check yields aggregate feasibility 0.685, compared with 0.389 without planning and 0.694 for repaired NSGA-II. The results support disjoint evaluation under the implemented load/outage proxies, not physical resilience superiority or active DER-uncertainty coverage.
